import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_92/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_92/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_92/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_92_2 and Source3_92_0 on movie_id
join_1 = pd.merge(source2, source0[['movie_id', 'title', 'video_release_date']], on='movie_id', how='left')

# Join the above result with Source3_92_1 on user_id
join_2 = pd.merge(join_1, source1[['user_id', 'age']], on='user_id', how='left')

# The target schema is:
# ['title': string, 'movie_id': integer, 'video_release_date': float, 'user_id': float, 'rating': float, 'unix_timestamp': float, 'age': float]

# Ensure correct dtypes and column order
# title: string
join_2['title'] = join_2['title'].astype(str)

# movie_id: integer
join_2['movie_id'] = join_2['movie_id'].astype(int)

# video_release_date: float (some are NaN, keep as float)
join_2['video_release_date'] = pd.to_numeric(join_2['video_release_date'], errors='coerce')

# user_id: float
join_2['user_id'] = join_2['user_id'].astype(float)

# rating: float
join_2['rating'] = join_2['rating'].astype(float)

# unix_timestamp: float
join_2['unix_timestamp'] = join_2['unix_timestamp'].astype(float)

# age: float
join_2['age'] = join_2['age'].astype(float)

# Reorder columns to match target schema
target_df = join_2[['title', 'movie_id', 'video_release_date', 'user_id', 'rating', 'unix_timestamp', 'age']]

# Save to the target path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_92/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_92/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_92/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_92/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_92_2 and Source3_92_0 on movie_id
joined_0 = pd.merge(source2, source0, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_92_1 on user_id
joined_1 = pd.merge(joined_0, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by 'title' and 'movie_id' (leftmost non-float unique columns in target schema)
# Aggregate other columns by mean to match target float columns
grouped = joined_1.groupby(["title", "movie_id"], as_index=False).agg({
    "video_release_date": "mean",
    "user_id": "mean",
    "rating": "mean",
    "unix_timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = grouped[["title", "movie_id", "video_release_date", "user_id", "rating", "unix_timestamp", "age"]]

# Write output to the specified path
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_92/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
